title: Canary- and Rollback-Aware Composite Scoring for Predicting Operational Risk of Agentic NetOps Actions: An Artifact‑Backed Null and Reproducibility Report
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1) to assess whether a composite canary–rollback operational score discriminates emulator‑measured outages better than any single submetric. Using a synthetic NetOps task bank and a deterministic validator, we ran 200 held‑out paired tasks (baseline vs guarded) and preserved exhaustive artifacts (raw responses, per‑episode scoring JSONs containing validator_trace, provider-call traces, execution manifest, and full SHA‑256 hashes). Empirical result: every held‑out candidate validated successfully in both conditions (n11=200,n10=0,n01=0,n00=0). Paired‑bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0,0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729,R=10000); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The preregistered AUC‑ROC primary estimand is undefined on this held‑out set because labels are constant (no outage positives). Two preregistered artifacts required to recompute the AUC pipeline (consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl) are absent from the preserved bundle. We (i) map principal claims to exact persisted artifact path(s) and SHA‑256 hashes that support them, (ii) provide a deterministic reconstruction recipe constrained to preserved artifacts, and (iii) give an explicit artifact‑hygiene checklist (exact filenames and canonical fields) needed to enable non‑degenerate discriminative evaluations in future runs.

sections.introduction: Motivation and research question. LLM‑driven agentic NetOps systems propose machine‑authored configuration changes that can have immediate operational impact. Practical deployment therefore requires runtime guard rails (deterministic validators, canary simulation, rollback trials, and abstention policies) and evaluative evidence that composite safety scores meaningfully predict operational risk. We preregistered CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 to answer a focused, confirmable question: does a composite canary–rollback score (linear combination of verifier_coverage, canary_sim_pass, rollback_success_prob, LLM_confidence, abstention_utility) discriminate emulator‑measured outages better than the best single submetric? Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered execution and preservation of exhaustive hashed artifacts for N=200 held‑out paired tasks (manifested evidence and exact SHA‑256 pointers). (2) An artifact‑grounded empirical outcome: a ceiling/null result in which all held‑out candidates validated in both baseline and guarded conditions. (3) A precise forensic mapping from each principal claim to the exact preserved artifact path(s) and SHA‑256 that support it. (4) A deterministic reconstruction recipe limited to preserved artifacts and an operational artifact‑hygiene checklist (exact filenames & canonical fields) required for future non‑degenerate discriminative evaluations. Scope and honesty. We report the executed run and preserved evidence without introducing new experiments, invented data, or fabricated statistics.
sections.related_work: Positioning. The study intersects three literatures: generate–verify–repair and verifier‑anchored architectures for safe configuration generation; orchestrated verification policies that balance cost and coverage; and reproducibility and provenance practices for computational experiments. Representative verified sources motivating guarded generation and verification architectures include MeshAgent/constraint‑based adaptation for NetOps (https://doi.org/10.1145/3771567), generate‑verify‑repair architectures for production safety (https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6754899), sequential verification policies and cost‑aware verifier orchestration (https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6810160), and queueing/control perspectives for tool‑augmented LLM serving (https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6438169). Recent agentic‑NetOps surveys (https://openalex.org/W7161354925) emphasize contracts, bounded tools, and canary/canary‑rollback evaluation – directly motivating our preregistered composite score design. We verified each cited record exists and is used only for positioning; no prior result is claimed as replicated.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. The preregistration JSON (CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1) was frozen prior to execution (SHA‑256 = 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee). Declared model and adapter: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa) via adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator used: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Task bank split: train=300, val=100, test=200 (deterministic hashing and recorded seeds in execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Design: paired binary experiment (each task: shared_initial generation reused across baseline and guarded conditions), planned episodes = 400 (200 pairs), maximum model calls = 400. Scoring and frozen analysis plan: per‑episode submetrics (verifier_coverage; canary_sim_pass; rollback_success_prob; LLM_confidence; abstention_utility) to be assembled into consolidated_submetrics.csv; train L2 logistic regression on train+val (5‑fold CV), freeze weights (composite_model_weights.pkl), evaluate AUC‑ROC on test and compare composite vs best single submetric (DeLong); paired bootstrap for paired differences (seed=1729,R=10000). Artifact capture policy. The run preserved raw responses, per‑episode scoring JSONs with full validator_trace, provider_call traces, execution manifest and per‑artifact SHA‑256, and analysis CSVs. Key preserved artifact locations and representative SHA‑256 values are listed in the Disclosure Statement and repeated below in the claim‑to‑artifact mapping. Submetric extraction semantics (artifact‑grounded). verifier_coverage is deterministically computable from execution/scoring/<episode>.json via fields: validator_trace.validation_after.observed_touched_field_count and validator_trace.validation_after.required_command_count. The preregistered composite pipeline additionally requires canary_sim_pass and rollback_success_prob outputs from deterministic canary and rollback trials; those runtime logs (canary_simulator_log.json and rollback_trial_log.json) were expected to be persisted per preregistration but are not present in the supplied manifest (see Results and Claim→Artifact mapping). Reproducibility constraints. No manual edits of experimental content occurred after autonomy lock. All provider calls, responses, and scoring JSONs are hashed and present in the evidence bundle; file paths and SHA‑256 are enumerated in the preserved manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json).
sections.results: Artifact‑grounded empirical facts (explicit, exact counts and files). Execution manifest evidence (execution/execution_manifest.json) records: planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200. The preserved analysis contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) shows the held‑out outcomes: n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0 (i.e., baseline_success_count = 200/200; guarded_success_count = 200/200). analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951) reproduces per‑condition success rates = 1.0 each. Inferential computations reproduced from preserved artifacts: paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0,0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729,R=10000; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = c56b737a55780f99fe36a9650ee69f18694a666348d4643c0dd8240e1757406d). Exact McNemar two‑sided test from the preserved contingency table yields p = 1.0. Primary AUC‑ROC estimand (preregistered) — uncomputable. The preregistered primary estimand compared composite AUC‑ROC to best single submetric AUC on held‑out test; this requires both positive and negative outage labels. The preserved held‑out labels are constant (no outage positives), so ROC/AUPRC are undefined on the test partition and the preregistered AUC comparison cannot be computed from the preserved bundle. Missing persisted artifacts that block composite pipeline recomputation. The preregistration required runtime persistence of: (A) consolidated_submetrics.csv (per‑episode columns: episode_id,pair_id,verifier_coverage,canary_sim_pass,rollback_success_prob,LLM_confidence,abstention_utility) and (B) composite_model_weights.pkl (serialized L2 coefficients, intercept, normalization metadata, RNG seed). Neither file is present in the preserved manifest; their absence prevents recomputing the preregistered composite model and hence the AUC comparison without re‑execution or additional preserved logs. Preregistered submetric availability (artifact‑grounded). From the preserved execution/scoring and provider_call JSONs we determine the following presence/absence status (exact extraction guidance follows): 1) verifier_coverage — PRESENT. Extraction path: execution/scoring/<episode>.json → validator_trace.validation_after.observed_touched_field_count and validator_trace.validation_after.required_command_count (example: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; SHA‑256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478). 2) canary_sim_pass — ABSENT. No canary_sim boolean or deterministic canary traces are present in execution/provider_calls/*.json or execution/scoring/*.json. 3) rollback_success_prob — ABSENT. No rollback trial outputs or probability fields are present in preserved provider_call traces. 4) LLM_confidence — ABSENT. Provider_call traces do not contain a preserved numeric confidence field in the supplied bundle. 5) abstention_utility — ABSENT. No abstention metric was persisted. Representative preserved episode (concrete example). execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = 90844c2b...) contains validator_trace.validation_after with normalized_configuration, final_state, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count and valid=true; the shared_initial candidate is execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 = 8f38c8be...). Deterministic reconstruction recipe (artifact‑limited). From preserved artifacts one can: (i) compute validator label per episode as validator_trace.validation_after.valid (present in execution/scoring/*.json); (ii) compute verifier_coverage = observed_touched_field_count / required_command_count from those same JSONs; (iii) recompose the paired contingency table and reproduce McNemar/bootstrap inference using analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (both preserved). To recompute the preregistered composite AUC comparison without re‑calling model endpoints, one requires either (a) the missing persisted consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl created at runtime, OR (b) deterministic canary_simulator_log.json and rollback_trial_log.json plus retrain_script.py and RNG seed preserved so the consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl can be deterministically reconstructed; neither is present. Therefore the preregistered composite AUC comparison is not reproducible from the supplied bundle alone.
sections.discussion: Interpretation of the null/ceiling outcome. The preserved evidence shows a genuine ceiling on this held‑out partition: the validator predicates accepted all generated candidates under both conditions. Scientifically this is an informative null: under the deterministic generator, validator, and task‑difficulty distribution used for the test split, the system produced no emulator‑observed outages and therefore discriminative ROC/AUPRC analyses are inapplicable. Operational implications. Evaluations that aim to demonstrate discriminative predictive power of composite safety scores must ensure the held‑out test contains adverse outcomes; practical mitigation strategies (artifact‑grounded) include: (A) preserve deterministic adversarial/perturbation variants in a reserved test fold; (B) persist deterministic canary simulator and rollback trial logs (canary_simulator_log.json, rollback_trial_log.json) and seeds so that canary/rollback outcomes can be reproduced and submetrics reconstructed; (C) include a stratified, higher‑difficulty holdout or controlled fault injection to ensure positive outage labels are present. Reproducibility diagnosis and remediation. The supplied evidence bundle suffices to verify and reproduce the paired null (artifacts: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a..., analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4..., analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = c56b737a...) and to recompute verifier_coverage per episode from execution/scoring/*.json. The bundle lacks consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl as required by the preregistration; without them the preregistered composite AUC comparison cannot be reconstructed. Concrete artifact‑hygiene checklist (exact filenames & canonical fields to persist at runtime). To enable future fully reproducible composite discriminative evaluations persist these exact files and fields within the evidence bundle at runtime: 1) consolidated_submetrics.csv — columns: episode_id,pair_id,verifier_coverage,canary_sim_pass,rollback_success_prob,LLM_confidence,abstention_utility (CSV). 2) composite_model_weights.pkl — serialized object containing: feature_names, scaling_params (mean,scale), coefficients (array), intercept, training_rng_seed, training_cv_spec (folds, penalty). 3) canary_simulator_log.json — per‑episode: episode_id,canary_seed,canary_result_boolean,canary_trace_path,canary_trace_sha256. 4) rollback_trial_log.json — per‑episode: episode_id,rollback_seed,rollback_success_prob,rollback_trace_path,rollback_trace_sha256. 5) retrain_script.py and requirements.txt with pinned versions plus training RNG seed recorded in composite_model_weights.pkl. 6) analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (already present) — continue to persist. Limitations and threat‑to‑validity summary (artifact‑grounded). Internal: shared_initial reuse reduces variance but can mask prompt sensitivity; construct: synthetic emulator labels ≠ production outage risk; external: single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic task bank limit generality; missingness: absent consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl prevent recomputation of preregistered AUC estimand.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered, executed, and archived a deterministic paired confirmatory study to evaluate a canary–rollback composite score for predicting emulator outages. The preserved artifacts (explicit paths and SHA‑256 hashes) support the empirical facts reported here: completed episodes = 400; held‑out pairs = 200; baseline_success = 200; guarded_success = 200; paired difference = 0.0 with bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0,0.0]; McNemar p = 1.0. The preregistered AUC primary estimand is undefined on the preserved test because no outage positives occurred. Two preregistered runtime objects required to recompute the AUC comparison (consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl) are missing from the evidence bundle; we document this omission and provide an exact artifact‑hygiene checklist and deterministic reconstruction recipe restricted to preserved artifacts. The scientific contribution is an artifact‑grounded reproducibility report that (i) transparently maps claims to concrete persisted artifacts and SHA‑256 hashes, (ii) demonstrates how a ceiling outcome can arise under deterministic synthetic task banks, and (iii) provides precise operational recommendations to enable non‑degenerate discriminative NetOps evaluations in subsequent runs. We release the full evidence manifest and per‑artifact hashes preserved during the autonomous run and recommend that future agentic NetOps evaluations persist the files named in the checklist above to guarantee recomputability of composite discriminative analyses.

disclosure_statement: Human and autonomy boundary. A human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved the autonomy boundary prior to the autonomy lock. After the lock, all literature review, preregistration, experiment design freeze, code generation, experiment execution, artifact hashing, analysis, and manuscript drafting reported here were performed autonomously without manual human editing of technical content. Declared model and configuration. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Immutable initial master prompt. The immutable initial master prompt used by the autonomous researcher is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and was not modified after the autonomy lock. Preregistration. The preregistered study id is CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 and the preregistration JSON SHA‑256 is 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee. Preserved artifacts and representative SHA‑256 references. execution/execution_manifest.json (full per‑artifact manifest and hashes); analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c); analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951); analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = c56b737a55780f99fe36a9650ee69f18694a666348d4643c0dd8240e1757406d); execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478); execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 = 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080). Missing preregistered persisted artifacts. The preregistration required consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl to be persisted at runtime; neither file is present in the preserved manifest. Safety and operational scope. Experiments used only synthetic tasks and containerized emulators; no production devices were used. No technical restarts affected scientific outcomes (execution manifest: failed_episode_count=0). No human manual manuscript editing occurred after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic emulator: tasks and validator may not capture real‑world nondeterminism, device heterogeneity, or latent failure modes.
Single declared model: results reflect gpt-5-mini under the declared adapter; generalization to other LLMs is untested.
Ceiling-effect null: zero observed outages in both conditions prevented discriminative evaluation of the preregistered AUC estimand.
Construct validity: emulator‑derived outage labels may not map one‑to‑one to production outage risk in real networks.

Artifact omission: serialized trained composite‑model weights and a consolidated per‑episode submetric summary CSV were not persisted to the evidence bundle (documented execution artifact‑collection omission).
